title: Golden Gate Assembly Protocol
author: N.J. Hillson
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6t4heqw
materials: NEB PNK enzyme is supplied with its PNK buffer and it does not contain the ATP required for the phosphorylation reaction. To simplify the reaction step, use T4 ligase buffer (instead of PNK buffer). T4 ligase buffer provides the appropriate amount (1mM ATP) of phosphate for the phosphorylation reaction.

steps.title: Measure DNA concentration
steps.instruction: Determine the concentration (ng / ml) of each DNA assembly piece using a spectrophotometer or equivalent method.

steps.title: Prepare assembly reaction mixture
steps.instruction: In a tube bring the total volume to 15 ml by adding: 100 ng linearized vector backbone, equimolar amounts of each additional assembly piece, 1.5 ml 10X NEB T4 Buffer, 0.15 ml 100X BSA (required for BsaI activity), 1 ml BsaI, 1 ml NEB T4 Ligase (2 × 10⁶ cohesive‑end units / ml), and sterile dH₂O up to 15 ml. Use a high‑concentration ligase; note that BsaI is only ~10 % active at 37 °C without BSA.

steps.title: Run thermocycler program
steps.instruction:
Program the thermocycler with one of the following options:
• Engler 2009 style: 25 cycles of 3 min @ 37 °C → 4 min @ 16 °C, then 5 min @ 50 °C, 5 min @ 80 °C, finish with 1 cycle.
• Engler 2008 style (modified): 1 h @ 37 °C, then 5 min @ 50 °C, 5 min @ 80 °C, finish with 1 cycle.
If any assembly piece contains an internal BsaI site, first silence it by point mutation; alternatively, omit the final 50 °C/80 °C ligation step when internal overhangs are incompatible.

steps.title: Transform assembly into competent cells
steps.instruction: Introduce 5 ml of the completed assembly reaction into 100 ml of competent E. coli (or an appropriate volume) and plate or recover as usual. Optionally run a diagnostic agarose gel to verify assembly success.

steps.title: Reconstitute dehydrated oligos
steps.instruction: For each dehydrated oligo (quantity given in nanomoles), add sterile, RNase/DNase‑free water equal to ten times the nanomole amount (µl) to obtain a 100 µM stock solution. Oligos may be supplied in tubes or 96‑well plates.

steps.title: Set up phosphorylation reaction
steps.instruction: For each forward (FW) and reverse (RV) oligo, combine in a 0.2 ml tube: 2 µl 100 µM oligo stock, 2 µl 10X T4 DNA ligase buffer, 15 µl sterile water, and 1 µl T4 Polynucleotide Kinase (PNK). Mix to a final volume of 20 µl.

steps.title: Incubate phosphorylation and store
steps.instruction: Incubate the 20 µl phosphorylation mix at 37 °C for 1 hour, then heat‑inactivate PNK at 65 °C for 20 minutes. Store the phosphorylated oligos at –20 °C until needed.

steps.title: Anneal phosphorylated oligos
steps.instruction: For each pair, mix 5 µl phosphorylated FW oligo, 5 µl phosphorylated RV oligo, and 90 µl sterile water (total 100 µl).

steps.title: Heat annealing reaction
steps.instruction: Place the 100 µl annealing mixture at 95 °C for 3 minutes. For more than ten reactions, use a thermocycler without a heated lid to simplify tube removal.

steps.title: Cool and store annealed oligos
steps.instruction: Allow the reaction to cool at room temperature for approximately 30 minutes to 1 hour, measure the concentration with a nanodrop, and store the annealed duplexes at –20 °C.
